land.text: Babylonia, restored as an independent kingdom by Nabopolassar

predecessors.note: Same state: a new (Chaldean) dynasty on the same land; the babylonia dossier ends in the same month.

land.text: the Assyrian heartland and "the lands west of the Euphrates" and the Levant that Babylon took in the partition

predecessors.note: The Neo-Babylonian Empire page lists the Neo-Assyrian Empire, the Kingdom of Judah and Philistia as predecessors.

land.text: the whole Neo-Babylonian territory, conquered by Cyrus in 539

successors.note: Babylon fell on 12 October 539 after the Battle of Opis; Cliopatria keeps the Neo-Babylonian row to -531.

capitals.name: Babylon (near Hillah)
capitals.note: Infobox "Capital: Babylon". Nabonidus lived for ten years at Tayma in northern Arabia (returned c. 543).

correction.text: Babylon and Nippur, "the cities of Babylon and Nippur"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -626..-621: Cliopatria has no shape for the first years; "In 626 BC, Nabopolassar assaulted and successfully seized the cities of Babylon and Nippur" and was crowned in November.

correction.text: Babylonia, most of it under Nabopolassar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -620..-613: "In 620 BC Nabopolassar seized control over much of Babylonia" (Babylonia page). Cliopatria's Babylonia -615 shape (152,403 km2) is the best proxy; it is part of the babylonia dossier's row.

correction.text: Babylonia and the Assyrian heartland after the fall of Nineveh

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -612..-606: after Nineveh (August 612) Babylon and the Medes split the Assyrian lands; Babylon held Babylonia and the Assyrian heartland. The page does not map the partition ("The Medes received the northern Zagros mountains").

correction.text: the empire after Carchemish: Babylonia, the Assyrian lands, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Jordan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -605..-601: Cliopatria's first Neo-Babylonian shape begins in -600, but Nebuchadnezzar "conquered all of Ha[ma]th" and beat Egypt at Carchemish in 605; this is the -600 shape five years earlier.

703,406 km2 (-600..-551): Iraq, Syria (142,636 km2), south-east Turkey (148,705 km2), Israel, Lebanon, Jordan, bits of Iran and Saudi Arabia. The infobox gives 500,000 km2 for 562, ratio 0.71 for this shape and 0.88 against the -550 shape; the page says Nebuchadnezzar's "borders of his empire, by the end of his reign, had not noticeably increased in size". Not contradicted.

569,654 km2 (-550..-541), ratio 1.14 against the infobox's 500,000 km2 for 562. The change from -600 loses 135,554 km2 in south-east Turkey and the upper Tigris; the page dates no loss (Cyrus's revolt of 549 ended the Median Empire).

569,354 km2 (-540..-531) is valid only to the fall of Babylon: "Babylon fell on 12 October" 539 and "Babylon never again attained the status of an independent state". The years -538..-531 belong to the Achaemenid Empire.

region.text: the cities of Babylon and Nippur

ledger.note: Nov. 626 BC: Nabopolassar is crowned King of Babylon. "In 626 BC, Nabopolassar assaulted and successfully seized the cities of Babylon and Nippur. In November 626 BC, Nabopolassar was crowned King of Babylon." Same state as Babylonia, now the Chaldean dynasty.
620 BC: Nabopolassar controls most of Babylonia. "In 620 BC Nabopolassar seized control over much of Babylonia." The Assyrian garrisons and local chiefs who held the rest are not named.

612 BC: Nineveh falls to the Medes and Babylonians. "In 612 BCE, after a siege lasting two months, the Medes and Babylonians captured Nineveh." The Neo-Babylonian page: attacks began in July or August 614, Nineveh was besieged June to August 612 and "the territory of the Neo-Assyrian Empire had been split between Babylon and the Medes"; Babylon took the heartland east of the Euphrates (reading; the page maps only the Medes' share).

region.text: Harran, the lands west of the Euphrates and the Levant

ledger.note: 609 BC: Harran and the west. Ashur-uballit II "was defeated at Harran in 609 BC"; Babylon took "Transpotamia" (the lands west of the Euphrates) and the Levant in the partition with the Medes, who "received the northern Zagros mountains".
604 BC: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Ashkelon. The page has the campaign "in 604 BC" and the city "plundered and levelled to the ground".

597 BC: Jerusalem is taken. Chronicle: "In the month of Addaru [early in 597 BC], the second day, he took the city and captured the king" (the page also has "In 598 BC"). Judah stays a vassal kingdom under Zedekiah, who "refused to pay tribute" in 589.
587 BC: Jerusalem is destroyed. "His 587 BC destruction of Jerusalem ended the Kingdom of Judah" (Nebuchadnezzar II page: "586 BC", "probably ended in the summer of 586 BC").

region.text: the Kingdom of Judah, with the governor Gedaliah at Mizpah

ledger.note: 587 BC: Judah becomes Babylonian territory. "His 587 BC destruction of Jerusalem ended the Kingdom of Judah"; some administration remained "under the governor Gedaliah, governing from Mizpah under close Babylonian monitoring".

region.text: Tyre, the island city under its own kings

ledger.note: 573 BC: Tyre surrenders. The city "eventually surrendered to him in 573 BC" after a siege the page gives as 13 years; the Nebuchadnezzar page: "The island portion of the city was left alone", and the island city continued "under vassal kings".

region.text: the conquered city of Tayma in northern Arabia

ledger.note: c. 553 BC: Nabonidus takes Tayma. He "settled for ten years in the conquered city of Tayma in northern Arabia" and returned c. 543; the year is derived (543 plus ten), the page dates no conquest.

region.text: the part of the -600 shape missing from the -550 shape (south-east Turkey and the upper Tigris)

ledger.note: Cliopatria's shape drops 135,554 km2 in -550 (the south-east Turkey and upper Tigris part of the -600 shape). The page names no loss; Cyrus's revolt against Astyages in 549 ended the Median Empire. Unattributed.

region.text: Tyre, the island city under its own kings

ledger.note: 539 BC (bridged): Tyre's tie ends with the empire. The pages give no end to the vassal kingship of Tyre after the 573 surrender ("under vassal kings"); the relation is closed at the fall of Babylon on 12 October. Page silent.

12 Oct. 539 BC: Babylon falls to Cyrus. The Battle of Opis was in 539 BC and Babylon fell "On 12 October" after the Euphrates was diverted; "Babylon never again attained the status of an independent state". Infobox end 539 BC.

wars.name: Nabopolassar's war of independence

zones.text: the Assyrian heartland: Assur (614), Nineveh (612), Harran (609)

wars.outcome: Nabopolassar took Babylon and Nippur (626) and most of Babylonia (620); the Medes and Babylon took Assur (614), Nineveh (612) and Harran (609) and divided the empire.

wars.name: Battle of Carchemish and conquest of Hamath
wars.outcome: Nebuchadnezzar "decisively defeated" Egypt at Carchemish; Necho II's forces "completely annihilated"; "Nebuchadnezzar conquered all of Ha[ma]th".
wars.note: The page does not say Egypt had held Syria before 605.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Philistine and Judean wars
wars.outcome: Ashkelon levelled in 604; Jerusalem taken in 597; destroyed in 587/586 after Zedekiah stopped paying tribute in 589.
wars.note: Judah's challenge to Babylon had begun "By 601 BC".

wars.name: Siege of Tyre
wars.outcome: Tyre "eventually surrendered to him in 573 BC"; the island city kept its own kings.
wars.note: The 13-year length "is only given by Flavius Josephus"; 585 is 573 plus 13.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Egyptian and Arabian campaigns
wars.outcome: "In the 601 BC campaign, Nebuchadnezzar departed from the Levant and then marched into Egypt"; "It is possible that Nebuchadnezzar campaigned against Egypt in 568-567 BC"; the attack was repelled. In 599 he raided the Arabs of the Syrian desert.

wars.name: Cyrus's conquest of Babylon
wars.outcome: The Battle of Opis in 539 and the fall of Babylon on 12 October after the Euphrates was diverted; Nabonidus was the last king.

certainty.note: All frontiers are approximate; the Median Wall "built to defend Babylonia against incursions from the north" (Nebuchadnezzar II page) marks the northern edge of the core but is not dated.

notes:
IDENTITY AND SPLIT. Cliopatria starts the Neo-Babylonian row in -600 and ends it in -531; the page dates it 626 (Nabopolassar's coronation, Nov.) to 539 (12 Oct.). The babylonia dossier ends in the same month, and Cliopatria's Babylonia -615 shape is used here for -620..-613. Four new keyframes (-626, -620, -612, -605) fill the years Cliopatria lacks.
AREA. Infobox "562 BC: 500,000 km2" vs Cliopatria 569,654 km2 (-550): ratio 1.14, within the factor of two; vs the -600 shape 703,406 km2, 1.41. No page lists the empire's borders; the shapes are not contradicted.
PAGES. 2 own pages (Neo-Babylonian Empire, Nebuchadnezzar II; budget 1-2) plus Babylonia and Neo-Assyrian Empire read for sibling dossiers. Not opened: Nabopolassar, Nabonidus, Siege of Jerusalem, Cyrus's conquest. Hence the Tayma and -550 events are confidence 1.
GAPS. The upper-Tigris and south-east Turkey land drawn to -551 and lost in -550 has no page; the partition of Assyria between Babylon and the Medes is mapped by the page only for the Medes ("the northern Zagros mountains"). The Jazira (Harran) is attributed to Babylon from 609 by the partition sentence about "Transpotamia"; the page is silent on the Jazira itself. Egypt's presence in Syria in 609-605 is not on the pages opened.
FOR OTHER DOSSIERS. achaemenid-empire (me-05): gain from this state on 12 October 539 (Cliopatria has it start in -550); median-kingdom (me-05): the northern Zagros share, Assur 614; twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt (me-03): Carchemish 605; kingdom-of-judah, philistia, phoenicia (me-04): the 604, 597, 587 and 573 events as mirrors.
GAZETTEER. Names the gazetteer lacks: Tayma (38.48 E, 27.63 N, used as a coordinate), Ashkelon (coordinate), Babylon (Al Hillah used). Regions "Assyria" and "Levant" exist.
